posts.text:
What a good AI receptionist does on a call.

1. Greets the caller by your business name
2. Answers the common questions
3. Collects the job details
4. Books a time on your calendar
5. Sends you a summary

The caller hangs up with an appointment, not a voicemail.

Which step matters most to you?

Listen to an AI receptionist handle a real booking call 🎧

It answers the caller's questions, checks open times, and puts the appointment straight on the calendar. No hold music. No voicemail.

Want to call it yourself?

Reply DEMO and I'll message you the test number.

Reviews belong on your homepage, not just on Google.

Put 3 real reviews near the top, with first names and the job done.

A stranger trusts a stranger who already hired you.

Are your reviews on your homepage right now?

Our own business line is answered by an AI receptionist.

If I'm on a call or it's 11 PM, it picks up, gets the details and sets up the follow up.

I built it for clients. Then I realized I needed it most.

Who answers your phone when you can't?

Honest question.

Would you be comfortable with an AI answering your business phone?

A) Yes, today
B) Maybe, if it sounds human
C) Only after hours
D) No way

Reply with your letter and why.

Your follow up is probably where the money is.

Most quotes never get a second touch. The customer was interested, got busy, and forgot.

One automatic text 2 days later wins back jobs you already thought were lost.

Do you follow up on every quote?

If your average job is worth $500, missing just 2 calls a week costs you $52,000 a year.

$500 × 2 calls × 52 weeks.

Answering every call isn't an expense. It's revenue you're already losing.

What's your average job worth? Reply with it and let's work out your yearly leak together.

Each service page should target one service in one city.

Not one page listing everything you do.

"Water heater repair in Orlando" beats "Our Services" every time someone searches.

How many service pages does your site have?

We build AI tools for the trades, not just websites.

One of ours helps electricians get answers and material lists fast, right from their phone.

The best AI isn't flashy. It saves a busy person time on a job site.

What task eats the most time on your jobs?

Want to see what fixing your lead flow would look like?

Reply WALKTHROUGH and I'll show you how the setup would work for a business like yours.

No pressure. Just a look.

Most businesses don't need a custom AI.

They need the boring stuff automated first. Lead replies. Reminders. Review requests.

Start there. Get the hours back. Then get fancy.

What's the first thing you'd automate?

The homepage layout we use for clients, top to bottom.

1. A clear headline that says what you do
2. The problem you solve
3. Proof, like reviews or results
4. One main button

Nothing else fighting for attention.

Drop your current headline below and let's rewrite it together.

Agents, every listing deserves its own website.

One address, one page, big photos and a button to book a tour.

It's easier to share, easier to remember, and it collects buyer leads for you, not the portal.

Do your listings get their own page?

We run an accessibility scan on every page we ship.

It checks that people using screen readers or keyboards can actually use the site.

It's the right thing to do, and it lowers your legal risk.

Has anyone ever checked your site for this?

Drop your website below and tell me the one thing you'd change about it.

I'll reply with whether I agree, and what I'd change first.

Reminder texts cut no shows.

One the day before. One the morning of. Both automatic.

Every missed appointment is a slot you could have filled.

Do you send reminders right now, or call by hand?

Off the shelf software works until your process gets a little complicated.

Then you end up working around the tool instead of the tool working for you.

Custom automations bend to how your business already runs.

Which app in your setup refuses to work with the others?

Your Google Business Profile might matter more than your website.

Hours, photos, services and reviews. That's what shows up first on a local search.

If it's half filled out, fix that before anything else.

When did you last update yours?

Our blog writes, checks and publishes new articles on a schedule.

AI drafts. Automated checks catch mistakes. Nothing goes live broken.

The point isn't more content. It's showing up on Google for the questions customers actually ask.

Does your site answer your customers' questions?

Running a home service business and want more Google reviews?

Our free 5 Star Review Kit shows you how to ask the right way.

Grab it here
evogencyglobal.com/free-review-kit

AI is only as good as the instructions behind it.

A receptionist that doesn't know your prices, service area or hours will sound smart and still get it wrong.

Setup is the work. The tech is the easy part.

What would your AI need to know about your business?

A real estate site shouldn't just mirror the MLS.

It needs three things.

1. Fast property search
2. Instant tour booking
3. A neighborhood report sent automatically the moment someone signs up

Agents, how many of your site visitors actually reach out?

Your website should tell visitors what to do next on every page.

Call. Book. Get a quote.

Pages that end with nothing to tap are dead ends.

Scroll to the bottom of your homepage. What's there?

For real estate, we build listing pages that do more than show photos.

Buyers book a tour right on the page. The agent gets the lead instantly.

The listing works for the agent around the clock.

Agents, where do your listing leads come from today?

What's harder for your business right now?

A) Getting leads
B) Answering them fast
C) Turning them into paying jobs

Reply with your letter.

After hours calls are often your best calls.

Someone calling at 9 PM about a leak isn't shopping around. They need help now.

Those jobs go to whoever answers.

How many of your calls come in after hours?

It's 9 PM. A homeowner calls about a leaking water heater. Your office is closed.

Here's what happens when an AI receptionist picks up.

1. It gets the details
2. It books the first open slot tomorrow
3. It texts you a summary

The job is yours before your competitor's voicemail even beeps.

What happens right now when someone calls your business after hours?

Build your site for a phone first.

Most local customers see it on their phone long before they ever see it on a computer.

Design for the thumb, not the mouse.

When did you last check your site on your phone?

The setup we use, start to finish.

Call comes in. AI answers. Details captured. Appointment booked. Summary sent to the owner.

The owner hears about the job after it's already on the calendar.

What would you do with the time that frees up?

Want this setup for your business?

Reply FRONT DESK and I'll show you how it would work with your calls, your hours and your calendar.

Your team shouldn't be your answering service.

Every time a tech stops a job to take a call, you're paying two people to do one thing badly.

Let the phone get answered without stopping the work.

Who answers calls at your business during the day?

3 things to check before Monday.

1. Does your contact form actually reach your inbox?
2. Is your phone greeting current?
3. Does your main button work on a phone?

Takes 10 minutes. Could save a week of lost leads.

Did you find anything broken? Tell me below.

Speed check for your Sunday.

Open your site on your phone using cell data, not Wi Fi.

Count the seconds until you can tap something.

Over 3 seconds? That's where your visitors are leaving.

What did you get?

This week we showed real systems doing real work. AI on the phones, chat on the site, leads landing in one place.

Next week I'm auditing websites for free and sharing what I find.

Want yours checked? Watch for tomorrow's post.

If you could fix one thing about how your business gets customers, what would it be?

One sentence. I read every reply.
